To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the upper limits of fluence for 20 GRBs are set at 99 % confidence level.
the fluence of the GRB counterpart with energy above 100 GeV is limited to be less than 1.2
the fluence upper limits for the 20 selected GRBs are in the range of (1.1–4.4) × 10−6 erg cm−2.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the search for GRB counterpart using the ARGO experiment.
the search of GRB counterparts in the TeV energy band, which is complementary to the searches in other energy bands.
the study of GRBs in the high energy range.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no evidence of GRB counterparts in the energy range from 1 GeV to 10 TeV in the data of ARGO‐Ybj experiment.
no significant gamma ray emission has been found by the ARGO‐ YBJ experiment for the selected GRBs in the energy range from 100 GeV to 1000 GeV.
the upper limits of fluence are not sensitive enough to constrain the GRB model.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
no significant excess is observed and the upper limits on the fluence for all the GRB counterparts are set in the energy range of 10 GeV–1 TeV.
no GRB counterpart was found in the ARGO‐field of view in the energy range 10 GeV–1 TeV.
no significant emission from the 20 GRB events has been found in the ARGO‐field of view.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ARGO‐ YBJ experiment is sensitive to GRB counterparts with a fluence of 10−4 erg/cm2 in the energy range from 100 MeV to 1 TeV.
the ARGO experiment is sensitive enough to search for GRBs in the energy range from 100 GeV to 100 TeV.
the ARGO‐ YBJ experiment is a very good candidate for GRB counterpart search.
